dedupe_keys.name: probabilistic forecasting of hourly emergency department arrivals gam and intermittent exponential smoothing models 48 hour horizon

description: This 2023 study in Health Systems by Bahman Rostami-Tabar of Cardiff University, Jethro Browell of the University of Glasgow and colleagues develops models that forecast how many patients will arrive at an emergency department in each hour of the next 48 hours, with a full probability distribution, not a single number. The article read on 2026-09-28 presents a model based on generalised additive models and a dynamic exponential smoothing model suited to intermittent counts, compares them with benchmarks including TBATS, Poisson regression, Prophet and an empirical distribution, and scores point accuracy with root mean squared error and distribution accuracy with quantile bias and pinball scores; the proposed models beat the benchmarks, and the authors argue they generalise to ambulance and clinical desk services. The data are hourly arrivals at one emergency department, whose flagged outliers include public holidays and a heavy snowfall in the UK. Coverage is the department studied, in the United Kingdom judging by the events cited. The article is open access and free to read on PubMed Central; whether data and code are released, and under which licence, was not read. Caveats: the models are tuned to one site's patterns. It supports capacity planning and emergency response studies, such as setting hourly staffing levels or anticipating demand surges during storms. Related record: the synthetic emergency healthcare services dataset.
